title: A thermal model permits cold ice at the warm-dust radii of Gaia20cdd and sets limits on extra heating
abstract: We test whether the reported small ice grains of Gaia20cdd must be farther from the star than its warm carbon dust. Mie absorption and energy balance give 90-127 K for pure ice spheres of radius 0.03-0.3 um at 2.5-4 au in two published stellar models. Different grain temperatures therefore do not require different orbital radii. A 0.1 um sphere needs a temperature below 129.68 K for an initial radius erosion time of 61 days in vacuum. At the matched single-star 2.5 au and binary 4 au points, additional absorbed power must stay below 0.00209 and 0.00365 times the incident bolometric stellar power. A 550 K blackbody radiation field has allowed intensity dilution below 0.00071 and 0.00099. These limits hold the ice emission efficiency fixed. They are not carbon mass fractions or measured dust geometry. We provide thermal and UV sensitivity tables, numerical checks, code and an external-input retrieval recipe. The ice identification, optical constants at low temperature, stellar UV light and grain contact remain uncertain. This calculation does not measure an ice lifetime or confirm a common dust location.
